newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money unchanged despite holidays.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money unchanged despite holidays.

text.p: Manila overnight money was unchanged at an average of 9.9375 percent on Monday even after banks covered five days of reserve positions, traders said.
Banks were closed on Thursday and Friday for the Easter holidays and they had to cover from Wednesday to Sunday.
"Lenders in the market lent for fear the Central Bank might close its overnight borrowing facility immediately," a foreign bank dealer said.
The market had 31 lenders and 19 borrowers, with volume lower at 10.076 billion from 10.891 billion pesos.
A dealer said only the small banks were the borrowers amid the high liquidity in the system.
In the secondary market, "there was no position taking," a dealer said, since rates have gone too low.
Banks were merely buying to satisfy clients' requirements, dealers said.
Traders said the benchmark 91-day T-bill rate could still move down to 9.6 percent in the auction later from last week's 9.724 percent.
